content: The protein known as ATP-binding cassette sub-family B member 7, mitochondrial, is encoded by the ABCB7 gene in humans. Function The protein encoded by the ABCB7 gene is a membrane-associated protein that belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily. ABC proteins are responsible for transporting various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. The ABC genes are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. This particular protein is a member of the MDR/TAP subfamily. Proteins in the MDR/TAP subfamily are involved in multidrug resistance and antigen presentation. The ABCB7 gene encodes a half-transporter that plays a role in the transport of heme from the mitochondria to the cytosol. Additionally, with iron-sulfur cluster precursors as its substrates, this protein may contribute to maintaining metal homeostasis. Clinical Significance Mutations in the ABCB7 gene have been associated with X-linked sideroblastic anemia with ataxia, a rare genetic disorder. Interactions The ABCB7 protein has been shown to interact with ferrochelatase, an enzyme involved in heme biosynthesis.
